To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temporal decline of protein sequence convergence is not an artifact of gene-tree discordance and that it is likely caused by an increasing effect of epistasis with increasing evolutionary distance between the lineages.

(1) the temporal decline of protein convergence in mammals is not explained away by gene tree discordance; (2) the temporal trend remains when the gene tree discordance is controlled; and (3) the trend is not caused by the genes whose genealogical histories are concordant or discordant with the species history.

the decline of convergence in more distantly related mammal species is not caused by gene tree discordance and that it is likely genuine, i.e., it is not caused by the methodological artifact of gene tree reconstruction.

the evolution of proteins, which are the functional molecules in the cell.

the impact of GTD on protein sequence evolution is complex.
epistasis does affect protein sequence evolution and that gene tree discordance is not a sufficient explanation for the temporal decline of protein sequence convergence in mammals.
the temporal decline of protein sequence convergence is at least partly genuine, but the extent of its genuine component and the relative contribution of epistasis to it are still open questions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal decline of protein convergence is not a simple function of GTD and that the impact of GTD on the temporal decline of convergent evolution is complex and requires further investigation.
epistasis is a real phenomenon that has an impact on convergence, and that the impact is not uniform across lineages.
the temporal decline of protein convergence is real, at least in part, and is caused by the epistasis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal decline of protein convergence should not be dismissed as a mere artifact of gene tree estimation.
the GTD effect on convergence is likely to be small and, thus, that it does not explain away the temporal decline of protein sequence convergence.
GTD cannot be used as a blanket excuse for the lack of temporal trends in protein sequence convergence.
